artifacts.summary: Rules the review unit, base resolution, ordering, restack disposition, handoff shape and platform support for cutting a PR stack from landing proofs by plumbing; fixture experiments E1 to E5; one user decision on what the bottom PR merges into.

user_decision.question: What does the bottom PR of a stack merge into? With isolation off the work is already on the integration branch, and in a fixture a review branch cut from the batch's cut point conflicted when merged into it.
options: A. A declared review base distinct from the integration branch (a new review_base key); PRs are mergeable, and a repository whose integration branch is its default branch gets a refusal and no PRs
B. The integration branch, as the task description says; PRs can be read and approved and are then closed, never merged
user_decision.recommended: A. A declared review base distinct from the integration branch (a new review_base key); PRs are mergeable, and a repository whose integration branch is its default branch gets a refusal and no PRs

memory_candidates.content: Two plumbing primitives build and maintain review branches without touching HEAD, the index or the working tree (git 2.54). Blob overlay (temporary GIT_INDEX_FILE, read-tree of the parent, update-index --cacheinfo per path from the task's end commit, write-tree, commit-tree, update-ref) is exact only when the parent is an ancestor of the branch the blobs come from: on a base that moved independently it silently replaces foreign edits to the same file. git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<old parent> <new parent> <commit> is a true three-way transplant, keeps foreign edits, exits 1 on conflict, and gave a tree equal to a full overlay rebuild after a squash-merged parent. git replay --onto also works but is marked EXPERIMENTAL and in 2.54 updates refs directly by default.

The push grant minted by hooks/please-grant.sh is bound to the SHA of HEAD at mint time, not to the pushed ref. Pushing a branch that is not checked out works as long as HEAD does not move within the 600 second window; a concurrent session committing to the checked-out branch invalidates the grant. /merge mints its grant for remote origin and the checked-out branch with no argument parsing, so /merge cannot push any other branch. PR creation (gh pr create, glab mr create) has no mechanical guard in hooks/ or scripts/; only the push is hook-enforced.
